stimulus.title: A particle moving along the x-axis

table.caption: The velocity of a particle, in meters per second, for 0 ≤ t ≤ 6 seconds, and its position at t = 0

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Is the speed of the particle increasing or decreasing at time $t = 2$? Give a reason for your answer.

accept: v(2) < 0 and a(2) < 0, with values or signs from the calculator

rubric.point: Increasing, because $v(2)$ and $a(2)$ have the same sign (both negative).
accept: speeding up because velocity and acceleration are both negative

parts.sample: $v(2) = 4\cos(1.8) - 0.4 \approx -1.309$ and $a(2) = v'(2) \approx -3.706$. Both are negative, so the speed is increasing at $t = 2$.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Find all times $t$ in $0 < t < 6$ at which the particle changes direction. Justify your answer.

accept: t = 1.653 and t = 5.548 (correct to three decimal places)

rubric.point: Justification: $v$ changes sign at each of these times (positive to negative at 1.653, negative to positive at 5.548).
accept: v changes sign at both times

parts.sample: Solving $4\cos(0.9t) - 0.2t = 0$ on the calculator gives $t \approx 1.653$ and $t \approx 5.548$. $v$ changes from positive to negative at $t \approx 1.653$ and from negative to positive at $t \approx 5.548$, so the particle changes direction at both times.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Find the position of the particle at time $t = 6$.

accept: x(0) plus the definite integral of v from 0 to 6

parts.label: d
parts.prompt: Find the total distance traveled by the particle over $0 \le t \le 6$. Find the average velocity of the particle over the same interval. Indicate units of measure.

accept: the sum of the absolute values of the integrals of v over [0, 1.653], [1.653, 5.548] and [5.548, 6]

rubric.point: Average velocity: $\frac{1}{6}\int_0^6 v(t)\,dt \approx -1.172$ meters per second, with units.

parts.sample: Total distance $= \int_0^6 |v(t)|\,dt \approx 15.974$ meters. Average velocity $= \frac{1}{6 - 0}\int_0^6 v(t)\,dt \approx \frac{-7.035}{6} \approx -1.172$ meters per second.
